Let's be honest, it's been a while since Zuckerberg took his bizarre cross-country tour that generated so many unique opportunities to show just how weird the guy is. He's been keeping a relatively low profile, and that's bad for fresh memes. Odds are he's going to continue to keep a low profile while his company is getting battered by various governments unhappy with some aspect of Facebook. With that in mind, here's some tools that a casual memetic engineer can use to keep the dream alive:

This is a typical fake facebook post generator. You need a source image as the user thumbnail, and if you're going for a post with a picture you'll have to upload that too. Be careful, these sites often have size caps that you don't find out about until AFTER you set it to process, and then poof goes your work. Keep the images saved locally, have your text on a file on your machine, just in case you have to rebuild. With all that said, the fake Facebook post can have a huge impact if done right, even if it's based on something as trivial as a shot of Zuckerberg's legs overextending as he walks.

There's the classic top/bottom meme. You get less visual bang for your buck, but you can get a solid meme with the set-up / punchline format. It's a fast one-two punch that requires little investment by the reader, increasing the odds they'll read it. The downside is they're less memorable and somewhat generic compared to the fake Facebook post.

The old-school motivational calendar format is a solid choice. The precursor of the top/bottom meme is a good bet for when you have a single line payload. It suffers from the same sense of being generic, but the wall calendar format may pop better with white-collar audiences.

Beyond all that, some general design advice:

1) If your audience is Normies, dropping Stormfront references probably won't serve your goal. Yes, yes, 14 words blah blah blah, Joe Sixpack took one look at your shit and closed the window in hopes no-one saw him looking at it, and he won't be back. You're preaching to sheep whose idea of edgy comedy is Louis CK. Know your audience.

2) Assume your audience hasn't got the time or the ability to read your sixty-page novella about how Zuckerberg once punched a baby in self-defense. If you're going for a big block of text you'd better be sure it is compelling enough to get someone reading and keep someone reading. That's a major issue: no-one is going to read your punchline if they don't engage in the first place. Less is More. Open strong, close strong.

3) The more you're going to write, the more you need to do your writing in something with a spelling checker and grammar checker first. Nothing kills a joke like having it all fucked up with typos and grammar mistakes. Spell check and grammar check are your friends.

4) Avoid white space in your pictures. Generally this isn't an issue with re-purposed photos, but if you've cobbled an image together any unused space should be minimized and balanced to avoid blank blocks. It's like a newspaper, space not used is money left on the table. Pack your shit and make it fit.
